notes.title: Friday the 13th Update 1.10: Nightmares and Scythes
notes.content:
[h2]The tolling of the bells has been answered by Death.[/h2][p][/p][previewyoutube="hQFwGQ-4jKE;full"][/previewyoutube][p][/p][p]One month after releasing Deck of Haunts, we're now ready to unleash the largest update yet.
It contains something a lot of you have been wanting, a higher difficulty![/p][p]Before we start off with giving you all of the info, we want to express a big thanks to our community, you give us motivation and energy to keep pumping out all of these updates.
And as always, if you like the game, a review is greatly appreciated, as it helps us a lot![/p][h3]Some of the highlights:[/h3][list][*][p]New game mode: Nightmare (Unlocked through playing a 28-day run first).[/p][/*][*][p]New trap cards and trap starter deck.[/p][/*][*][p]Crypt room and Grim Reaper (Unlocked through completing Nightmare).[/p][/*][*][p]New achievement.[/p][/*][*][p]Portraits of dead humans now disappear to make room.[/p][/*][*][p]New traits.[/p][/*][*][p]Raised the level cap from 10 to 12.[/p][/*][*][p]Most importantly, we added "Jason" to the pool of names for humans, it is Friday the 13th, after all.[/p][/*][/list][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45227801/7c25ee8c787681ad6908be5195382d0c5e70e874.jpg"][/img][/p][p][/p][h2]For those that want to know more, let's dive a little deeper.[/h2][p][/p][h3]Nightmare[/h3][p]Instead of just scaling some numbers to make the game more difficult, we've made an entirely new game mode: [b]Nightmare[/b].[/p][p]In Nightmare, you will have to survive 13 Nightmares consisting of 13 nights each.
During those nights you will encounter increasingly difficult curated groups of humans, some of them even containing new traits.
To make matters even more dangerous, every Nightmare will have a specific new modifier applied to it, which will carry over to the next Nightmare.[/p][p]A [b]new mechanic & professional scythe wielder[/b] has also been introduced in Nightmare: the [b]Grim Reaper[/b].
Whenever you kill or drive a human insane, you will collect a soul.
Once you've filled up your meter to 13, you can exchange those souls for a visit from the Grim Reaper, who will Harvest a human in your house of your choosing.[/p][p]If you can survive the final Nightmare, 13, you will have won over the confidence in your haunting skills of the Grim Reaper, and you will be able to permanently add them to your house in other game modes with the [b]Crypt room[/b] that you'll unlock.[/p][p][b]These are the extra unlocks you can achieve in the Nightmare mode:[/b][/p][list][*][p]Upon finishing the first Nightmare: 
- Card: Corpse Explosion.[/p][/*][*][p]Upon finishing the final Nightmare:
- Room: Crypt.
- Card: Sleep Paralysis.
- Achievement.[/p][/*][/list][h3]Trap deck[/h3][p]Upon reaching XP-level 12, you will unlock the new Trap deck.[/p][p]To make trap decks more viable, we've added 5 new trap cards:[/p][list][*][p]Leaking Rust[/p][/*][*][p]Improvised Snare[/p][/*][*][p]Collective Toll[/p][/*][*][p]Amplify Agony[/p][/*][*][p]Dragged Under[/p][/*][/list][h3]Some smaller additions[/h3][p]For some quality of life and more polish, we've added some other things to the game, such as:[/p][list][*][p]Death animation of the heart, when you lose a night.[/p][/*][*][p]Removal of portraits of dead humans.[/p][/*][*][p]Setting a counter of turns on humans with the "Helpline" trait.[/p][/*][/list][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45227801/2366b65e90aedfd00231a1dddf44ac3281380d14.gif"][/img][/p][h2]The full changelog.[/h2][p][b]Changes[/b][/p][list][*][p]Added Hard mode with curated nights.[/p][/*][*][p]Added Nightmare mode with curated nights .[/p][/*][*][p]Added Trap Deck to deck selection.[/p][/*][*][p]Added new Cards:[/p][list][*][p]Leaking Rust[/p][/*][*][p]Improvised Snare[/p][/*][*][p]Collective Toll[/p][/*][*][p]Amplify Agony[/p][/*][*][p]Dragged Under[/p][/*][*][p]Corpse Explosion[/p][/*][*][p]Sleep Paralysis[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Added Crypt Room.[/p][/*][*][p]Moved modifier/totem selection to the Deck selection screen.[/p][/*][*][p]Added an Achievement for Completing Nightmare mode.[/p][/*][*][p]Removed portraits of dead Humans.[/p][/*][*][p]Added death animation for the heart.[/p][/*][*][p]Balance cards:[/p][list][*][p]Deepening Shadows: Is now a rare card instead of uncommon[/p][/*][*][p]Unending Madness: Now costs 2 AP (From 1)[/p][/*][*][p]Triskaphobia: Upgraded version now costs 2 AP, Drain 2 thrice instead of 3 AP, Drain 3 thrice[/p][/*][*][p]Cascading mechanism: Now costs 1 AP (from 2)[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Added new traits:[/p][list][*][p]Martyr: Adds a useless card to your deck for the rest of the night when killed.[/p][/*][*][p]Destined: Dies upon reaching the Heart, takes max 1 damage 1 drain per turn.[/p][/*][*][p]Wary: Flees at the sight of insane humans.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Bell Crush ignores Traits that limit damage.[/p][/*][*][p]New basic room floor material during the day phase, also increasing its performance.[/p][/*][*][p]Update the amount of turns until an extra Human spawns for the Helpline Trait in the Human portraits.[/p][/*][*][p]Raised Level cap to 12.[/p][/*][*][p]Added “Jason” as name to the name-pool.[/p][/*][/list][p][b]Fixed Bugs[/b][/p][list][*][p]Fixed an issue where undo didn’t always work properly for room active).[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed Storage Room not being selectable with a controller for cards that don’t already target it.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed Under Fate’s Spell Hex count requirement is not the same as trait still spawning new Humans after the Human with the trait is killed.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed controller scrolling on Unlocked Cards screen.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed Card selection highlight disappears when notes.title: Upcoming Friday the 13th Update
notes.content:
It is almost time for a Nightmare to begin. In this case, you will be the one doing the haunting.

Post release we've been pushing out update after update, multiple times a week, leading the game into a direction based on your feedback.
But now, for our [b]"1 month anniversary"[/b] we're saving up some time to bring you something with a little bit more "oomph"!

On [b]Friday the 13th[/b] of June (how could we ignore such a date...) we'll be releasing the biggest update for Deck of Haunts yet.

Without giving away too much: there will be a new mode, where something "familiar" will be lurking about. Giving you a helping hand... if you are willing to offer up something in return.

Always wanted to try a Sanity or Damage driven deck? Time to try that out.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45227801/e46eec5ded8d93541e145a24eddbc9be3de12c65.gif[/img]

Apart from the starter decks (more of them to come as well in the future!), we've also spent some time on revamping the runs themselves.
Added to the now "Classic" very first run, where you previously could only re-run pretty much the same thing (albeit with some minor variation in stats/human amount/traits), we now have a run-system that will, every night, pick from a selection of more curated nights.

So, where in one run you might have a night where you get a solid group of high health regenerative humans with doctor bags that spawn in just 1 wave, in the next run that very same night might instead have you encounter 6 waves of fragile, steadfast humans with a compass.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45227801/6e50b2c2e824c0709cdf236ed187b081ad24dfd9.gif[/img]

The beauty of this system is, that we can keep on adding different curated runs into the mix to make sure you get an increased amount of variations in your runs!

notes.title: Journey of Deck of Haunts and the 5-headed Mantis team, from prototype to 1.0
notes.content:
[b]Hello world... we did it, we made a game and shipped it![/b]

First of all, we cannot express our gratitude enough for all the players that joined us on this journey from prototype to Deck of Haunts 1.0. (And now beyond... V1.01-1.02-1.03-...)
You have given us motivational and energy boosts along the way and are making sure we're going in the right direction with all the feedback that you're sharing on Steam, Discord and social media.

We are still actively working on making Deck of Haunts better every day, and are committed to keep pushing out updates in the near future and beyond. For all of you that left all those nice reviews and messages on the discussions forum, a big thank you from the entire team! ❤️

[b]Now, how did we get here?[/b]

It started off in late 2019, where the very first concept of Deck of Haunts was laid out, right before the strangeness of 2020 came to haunt us all.

We felt we were onto something with that concept. Mind you, it was a time before the market was flooded with a ton of deck builders.
Of course it would have been nice to start work on Deck of Haunts right away, but at the time we didn't have the budget or ideal team configuration to bring it to completion.

During 2020-2021-2022-2023 we, as so many other indie studios, went full throttle on work for hire for other companies and game studios. Starting off with all the assignments we could get (think VR training for factories to configurators for conventions), we luckily could transition fulltime into the games industry with all of our work for hire assignments.

Then... at the turn of the new year, 2024, we felt we were finally ready to tackle that concept that we had been dreaming of since late 2019, Deck of Haunts.

After securing the budget that was needed to sustain our 5-headed team during a little more over a year development, we released the breaks on the production train and started work on our haunted domain!

[i]The first publicly playable build of Deck of Haunts at GDC[/i]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45227801/cc6cf02cd3f08c60f8f961bd34f11bb0b5118570.jpg[/img]

[b]The important milestones we hit during 2024:[/b]
[list]
[*] GDC: The first publicly playable (by press & publishers) build of Deck of Haunts during a pre-mixer
[*] Publishing deal with Dangen Entertainment
[*] Game Force: The first player based convention where the game was playable for 2 days
[*] Release of the Steam store page
[*] Throwing out the first iteration of the demo into the world (scary!)
[*] Growing interaction on the Deck of Haunts Discord
[/list]
[i]Deck of Haunts cards turned to life as business cards[/i]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45227801/8f0ed997031c4be7ed2820cfff60411363e7fe66.jpg[/img]

[b]Now, we've just passed our most important milestone... the Deck of Haunts 1.0 release![/b]
As a team we feel like we were able to make a fun core game loop, dressed up in a neat gritty Art Deco styling.
We definitely want to steadily push out updates for the game, and build on it, together with the player base.
We have a ton of ideas of where to go from here, so, lets go!

[b]Some thoughts after we asked ourselves the question: What did we like the most during the road from prototype to Deck of Haunts 1.0?[/b]

I loved to see how we, as a freshly put together team during the work for hire years, grew into a well oiled game production machine during the work for Deck of Haunts.
We learned really well how to communicate with each other and streamline our individual thoughts and ideas into 1 vision. (And I loved to make humans explode in to bloody mists when you harvest them, of course.) 
- [i]Philippe, Producer & VFX Artist[/i]

What I enjoyed most during the development was the rapid progress we made in the first couple of months with the full team. We started from a simple prototype and it seemed like every week we had so much more than the week before. It's mind-blowing looking back at some of the early builds and seeing how far we have come today.
- [i]Tim, Senior Programmer[/i]

One of the most interesting and also most difficult aspects of the development of Deck of Haunts is its rather unique concept. It certainly is mostly a roguelike deckbuilding game, but also has many elements of a tower defense, of house building and on top of that, you play as a stationary villain. 
That means a lot of tropes and design ideas might not necessarily work for this game and thus most design decisions cant simply lean on "what has worked before". Which has meant that team meetings and discussions about which direction to take the game have always been great fun and filled with so many ideas.
Pushing out the demo was also a huge help in that regard. There was so much feedback which helped steer the direction of some of the ideas that were more difficult to nail down. Like the house building.
- [i]Bram, Programmer & Designer[/i]

There were a lot of cool things that happened during the production of Deck of Haunts. I had the opportunity to present Deck of Haunts to the public together with San on GameForce which was definitely a fun experience. It was my first time to stand at a booth, and to see people playing the game you worked on as a team was really cool to see. One more thing that stands out for me is that we tackled each step together, every member of the team has a voice in the design of the game which I think was very valuable and also an enjoyable process. We built this game together and it really felt like that. Kudos to the team for that one, it was a fun year!
- [i]Willem, 3D & SFX Artist[/i]

What I liked about the development was the incredible speed at creating new mechanics and iterating on existing ones. Every meeting felt like we were heading another step in the right direction.
- [i]San, Senior 3D Artist & Card Designer[/i]

If you have any questions for us, regarding the game, the team or the weather here in Belgium, feel free to ask them here or on our Discord, and we'll make sure to respond.

And as always, if you like the game and want to support it, make sure to leave a review, it helps more than you can imagine!

notes.title: Deck of Haunts - Dev Blog #2 - The Art Style by San Nollet
notes.content:
Hi everyone! I'm San, the art director of Deck of Haunts, and in this developer blog, I'll be taking you on a visual tour of our haunted mansion. Don't forget to bring your sanity with you on the way out—you don’t want to lose it. Let's begin.

[h1]The Foundation[/h1]

Down here in the basement is where we started laying the foundation of the whole game—including the art. When we began the project, we had to decide how to best approach the visuals. Early on, we discussed what emotions the game should evoke in the player. This gave us plenty of clues about how the art style could reinforce those feelings. As a small team with some experience, we wanted something that looks appealing yet achievable. While AAA graphics with highly polished assets were outside our scope, we aimed for more than simple indie visuals to reach a broader audience. 

From those meetings and brainstorms, we settled on a few core concepts. The first one is the power fantasy of being an evil haunted house. That means a dark color scheme with unsettling lighting, sharp corners everywhere to indicate the danger of the house, and dark, looming shadows in the corner of every room.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45227801/2a91b6c2e743cbeb2ea014ca32ca706e6adea126.png[/img]
[i]Our color palette created from movie stills[/i]

The second one was adding our own spin to those horror tropes: an art-deco mansion as a sort of familiar-yet fresh visual flavor for the haunted house. We chose this style not only because we love art deco,  but also because it’s sharp corners and patterns fit in well with our shape philosophy.

Lastly, we added a comic-book effect that gives outlines and more texture to all our assets. This makes them more visually appealing and does most of the heavy lifting in making all the assets coherent and engaging.

These combined concepts should provide an interesting hook when people see the game for the first time, while still engaging enough to keep those people immersed even after many hours of playtime.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45227801/3fc51201003976c189675e83d676b39b5e29b5a4.png[/img]
[i]One of the first visual iterations for Deck of Haunts[/i]

[h1]Into the frying pan[/h1]

Let’s head back to the main floor into the kitchen, where we’re currently cooking up all those concepts into an actual art style. Too many cooks spoil the broth (although in this house broth is better with some extra cooks in there), so thankfully with our small talented team we can discuss and progress very fast when making the art. Let’s take a look at the specific challenges our game brings.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45227801/4f2ac12042fede79da4989ab97a1d7105b5584c6.png[/img]
[i]The current state of our game[/i]

[b]The Pros[/b]
[list]
[*]Single Location — Since we only have one area in the game we don’t need to worry about creating a million objects or multiple locations with specific set dressing. This saves a lot of time in terms of unique assets and areas we need to make for the game.
[*]Assets have great efficiency — Most of the stuff we make will be seen by the player. If you suddenly decide to stop playing or rush through certain parts there wont be any skipped areas where we painstakingly created tons of unique assets for — a great benefit of having a tight gameplay loop.
[/list]
[b]The Cons[/b]
[list]
[*]Everything changes all the time — Since the house is built dynamically, we have fewer “cheating” options compared to static environments. Baking (more cooking references, yay!) light and shadows is very hard to do this way. Using real time lighting looks nicer but drains a lot of computing power on your device and might not work on lower-end devices.
[*]Partly random generated — The players will be making a lot of custom shapes with the rooms so sometimes it’s tricky to anticipate all the layouts and still make it look good in every way.
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45227801/d38d0767665d9f85bfc8f0dd1ec66b1d95ac587e.png[/img]
[i]Testing big room shapes[/i]

We’re still polishing the art but the feedback on our visuals has been amazing so far! A good indication that we’re achieving what we set out to do from the start.

[h1]Through the roof[/h1]

[i]Slaps roof of hou-[/i] wait, we don’t actually have a roof yet. 

We’re putting the last finishing touches on the house the coming months. Loads more rooms, specific objects, shader tweaks, special effects, etc. We’re *almost* done but still putting the final polish on everything and everyone. Thank you for reading and next time I will be delving deeper into the UI of the game! Time to pack our coats and sanity and hea- wait anyone smell that? Oh well must be my imagination. Until next time!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45227801/0a7dd00eeaa086628513e34bffb55bc4b289236e.png[/img]

notes.title: Welcome to Deck of Haunts!
notes.content:
Hello everyone!

We're [b]Mantis Games[/b], a small development studio in Belgium. We're thrilled to welcome you to our Deck of Haunts Steam page!

After working on several other external titles and helping the dreams of others become a reality, we have now conjured up our own: [b]Deck of Haunts[/b].

What would it be like to play as a haunted house and be the actual villain in a game? 
[b]Deck of Haunts[/b] is our take on that question.

In [b]Deck of Haunts[/b], you'll be able to manifest and transfigure your evil domain into the mortal world, where you will lure hapless humans towards their doom. Harvest the essence of your unwilling victims that enter your art deco bowels and use it to get a greater grip on their world. 

We invite you to step into a thrilling new take on the deckbuilding roguelike genre. Please consider [u]wishlisting[/u] [b]Deck of Haunts[/b] to keep up to date on its development and release. We can't wait to see the doom you'll unleash!
